s.t: Sales reported by our non-U.S. subsidiaries comprised $3,211, or 43%, of our 2025 consolidated sales of $7,500.
Ford Motor Company (Ford) and Stellantis N.V. (Stellantis) were the only individual customers accounting for 10% or more of our consolidated sales in one or more of the past three years.
Our 10 largest customers collectively accounted for approximately 76% of our sales in 2025.
Sales to our ten largest customers accounted for 76% of our overall sales in 2025.

Sales to major customers — Ford Motor Company (Ford) and Stellantis N.V. were the only individual customers to whom sales have exceeded 10% of our consolidated sales in one or more of the past three years.
However, some of our operations remain dependent on single sources for certain raw materials.

The extent of the impact of a pandemic on our business and financial performance, including our ability to execute our near-term and long-term operational, strategic, and capital structure initiatives, will depend on the duration and severity of the pandemic, which are uncertain and cannot be predicted.
We operate in 24 countries around the world and we depend on significant foreign suppliers and customers.
We depend on our subsidiaries for cash to satisfy the obligations of the company.
Our cash flow and our ability to meet our obligations depend on the cash flow of our subsidiaries.
Labor stoppages or work slowdowns at Dana, key suppliers or our customers could result in a disruption in our operations and have a material adverse effect on our businesses.
We and our customers rely on our respective suppliers to provide parts needed to maintain production levels.
We all rely on workforces represented by labor unions.
As a result, we are dependent on single sources of supply for some components of our products.

If we were to experience a significant or prolonged shortage of critical components from any of our suppliers, particularly those who are sole sources, and were unable to procure the components from other sources, we would be unable to meet our production schedules for some of our key products and to ship such products to our customers in a timely fashion, which would adversely affect our sales, profitability and customer relations.

The launch of new business is a complex process, the success of which depends on a wide range of factors, including the production readiness of our manufacturing facilities and manufacturing processes and those of our suppliers, as well as factors related to tooling, equipment, employees, initial product quality and other factors.

The principal sources of liquidity available for our future cash requirements are expected to be (i) cash flows from operations, (ii) cash and cash equivalents on hand and (iii) borrowings from our Revolving Facility.
